parameters.content:
## Generate invoice PDFs from Google Sheets and deliver via Gmail and Slack

### Who's it for

Freelancers and small studios who bill the same clients every month and still assemble invoices by hand. If your billable work already lives in a spreadsheet, this closes the gap between that sheet and a sent invoice.

### How it works

On the 1st of each month it reads your billable lines from Google Sheets, groups them by client, totals each group and renders one branded PDF invoice per client. Each invoice is archived to Google Drive, emailed to the client as an attachment, and reported to Slack — one message per invoice.

Table rows are built in a Code node rather than in the template, because the rendering service substitutes values and does not loop. The HTML is posted to an HTTP endpoint that returns a signed link, and a second request downloads it as a file so Drive and Gmail both receive the same binary.

### How to set up

1. Create a sheet with the columns `client`, `client_email`, `description`, `qty`, `unit_price`.
2. Put your company name, tax rate and payment terms in the **Set invoice defaults** node.
3. Add a Header Auth credential named `Authorization` with the value `Bearer YOUR_KEY`.
4. Choose your Drive folder and Slack channel.
5. Run once manually before turning the schedule on.

### Requirements

Google Sheets, Google Drive, Gmail and Slack credentials, plus an API key for the rendering endpoint (a free tier is available).

### How to customize

Swap Google Sheets for Airtable, Postgres or your billing system — only the first node changes. Edit the schedule to bill weekly. The template sets `thead { display: table-header-group }` so column headers repeat on every page and `tr { break-inside: avoid }` so no line is cut at a page break; keep both if your invoices run long.

## Step 1: Read the billable lines

A monthly schedule starts the run. Company name, tax rate and payment terms live in one Set node so they are edited in a single place, then the billable rows are read from your Google Sheet.

## Step 2: Build the rows and render

Lines are grouped by client, totalled and turned into table markup in the Code node. The HTTP request posts that HTML with the data and gets back a signed link, which the second request downloads as a file.

## Step 3: File it, send it, report it

The PDF is archived to Google Drive and emailed to the client as an attachment in parallel, so both get the same binary. Slack then receives a one-line summary per invoice.
